content.doc_md:
## Tutorials

The QUOTENAME() function returns a Unicode string with delimiters added to 
make the string a valid SQL Server delimited identifier.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT QUOTENAME('abcdef');

---

QUOTENAME(
string, quote_char
)

---

SELECT QUOTENAME('abcdef', '()');
```

## Tutorials

The REPLACE() function replaces all occurrences of a substring within a string, with a new substring.

Note:The search is case-insensitive.

Tip:Also look at theSTUFF()function.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT REPLACE('SQL Tutorial', 'T', 'M');

---

REPLACE(
string
,
old_string
,
new_string
)

---

SELECT REPLACE('SQL Tutorial', 'SQL', 'HTML');

---

SELECT REPLACE('ABC ABC ABC', 'a', 'c');
```

## Tutorials

The REPLICATE() function repeats a string a specified number of times.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT REPLICATE('SQL Tutorial', 5);

---

REPLICATE(
string, integer
)

---

SELECT REPLICATE(CustomerName, 2)
FROM Customers;
```

## Tutorials

The REVERSE() function reverses a string and returns the result.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT REVERSE('SQL Tutorial');

---

REVERSE(
string
)

---

SELECT REVERSE(CustomerName)
FROM Customers;
```

## Tutorials

The RIGHT() function extracts a number of characters from a string (starting from right).

### Code Examples

```
SELECT RIGHT('SQL Tutorial', 3) AS ExtractString;

---

RIGHT(
string
,
number_of_chars
)

---

SELECT RIGHT(CustomerName, 5) AS ExtractString
FROM Customers;

---

SELECT RIGHT('SQL Tutorial', 100) AS ExtractString;
```
